items.label: FIGURE 3.15
items.title: Amounts of primary energy and generation of electricity from fossil sources need to decline massively to reach net zero by 2050 (continued)
items.content: The figure displays four stacked area charts representing electricity generation (in exajoules) for different income groups: High-income, Upper-middle-income, Lower-middle-income, and Low-income. Each chart shows the transition from 2020 to 2050. Legend: Fossil (blue), Nuclear (orange), Renewables (red). Trends: In all income groups, the fossil fuel component (blue) declines significantly by 2050, while the renewable component (red) increases to become the dominant source of electricity generation. High-income: Fossil starts at approx. 25 exajoules in 2020 and drops to near zero by 2050. Upper-middle-income: Fossil starts at approx. 40 exajoules in 2020 and drops to near zero by 2050. Lower-middle-income: Fossil starts at approx. 15 exajoules in 2020 and drops to near zero by 2050. Low-income: Fossil is a very small component, declining to near zero by 2050. Source: NGFS 2023. Note: NGFS = Network for Greening the Financial System. Primary energy and the generating of electricity (in exajoules) are plotted and come from the NGFS Net Zero 2050 scenario.
